summary: Willard L. Johnson was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oberlin College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he held faculty posts at CSU Long Beach, San Diego State, Del Mar College, and Oberlin College.

Philosopher and linguist Willard Van Orman Quine studied at Oberlin, Harvard under Alfred North Whitehead, and under Rudolf Carnap. He served in the U.S. Navy and spent his career primarily at Harvard (1933–1978), holding the Edgar Pierce Chair.

Indologist Willem Bollée studied at Utrecht University under doctoral supervisor Jan Gonda, and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He served on the faculties of the University of Münster (1971–1978) and Heidelberg University (1976–1993).

Indologist and linguist Willem Caland earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Carel Gabriel Cobet and studied with Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. After teaching at Stedelijk Gymnasium Breda, he served as Chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University from 1906 to 1930.

Willem Frederik Stutterheim was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He studied at Utrecht and Leiden under Nicolaas Johannes Krom, later directing Surakarta College (1926–1936) and the Dinas Purbakala (1937), after serving in the Oudheidkundige Dienst.

Linguist Willem Lodewijk van Helten earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. Following a post at Gymnasium Erasmianum, he served as professor of Dutch language and literature and Old Frisian at the University of Groningen (1882–1911).

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and archaeology who studied at Leiden University between 1971 and 1983. He has held academic posts at Leiden University and the University of Indonesia.

William A. Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has held posts at the University of Virginia, Dharma Drum Institute, and Chung-Hwa Institute.

William Abbott Oldfather studied at Hanover College, Harvard University, and the University of Munich. A scholar in linguistics and other fields, he held faculty posts at Northwestern University (1903–1909) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1909–1945).
William Austin Montriou worked in Indology and law. His career included serving as an advocate at the Calcutta High Court and as Professor of Law and Jurisprudence at Presidency University.
William Blackstone was educated at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College, Oxford. He held an academic post at the University of Oxford from roughly 1758 to 1766.

Linguist and Indologist William Bright studied at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held posts at Deccan College, the U.S. Department of State, UC Berkeley, UCLA (1959–1988), and the University of Colorado Boulder (1988–2006).

Historian and sinologist William C. Kirby studied at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn. He served as a professor and dean at Washington University in St. Louis and later became a dean and center director at Harvard.

Indologist and linguist William Carey studied under Golok Nath Sharma and Ramram Basu. He founded the Baptist Missionary Society, Serampore College, and Serampore Mission Press, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Fort William College (1801–1830).

William Carlson Smith, active in Indology and other fields, studied at Grand Island College, the University of Southern California, and the University of Chicago. He conducted educational work for the American Baptist Missionary Union from 1912 to 1915.

Indologist William Chambers served as a political servant for the East India Company, worked as an interpreter for the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (1775–1792), and was a member of The Asiatic Society (1784–1793).
Indologist William Charles Macready was educated at Christ Church and the East India Company College. In 1854, he served as an Assistant Government Agent in the Ceylon Civil Service.

William Chittick, a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, completed his studies at the University of Tehran. He held positions at Sharif University of Technology, University at Albany, and Stony Brook University as SUNY Distinguished Professor.
Indologist and linguist William Doderet earned an M.A. from Balliol College, Oxford, in 1880. He subsequently served as University Teacher of Marathi at the University of Cambridge from 1910 to 1919.
Indologist William Douglas Penneck Hill studied as a scholar at King's College, Cambridge. He subsequently served as an Assistant Master at Eton College and as Principal of Jay Narayan Inter College.
